answer: Each agent must lock tokens in a vault before it can submit bids, and the protocol caps each identity’s influence by its locked stake rather than its account count. A raven-like newcomer can mint many identities, but each needs its own funded lock; splitting one balance does not multiply voting weight, while funding more identities ties up more capital. The mesa of validators can slash a lock when an agent double-signs, so a sybil attacker pays both an opportunity cost and a measurable penalty for abuse.
